373.h: The Federal University of Agriculture, Mubi (FUAMB) is a public university owned and run by the Federal Government. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2023.
373.a: As a university of agriculture, its programmes centre on agriculture and related sciences.
373.c: It is located in Mubi, Adamawa State, in north-eastern Nigeria.

374.h: The Federal University of Education, Zaria (FUEZ) was created from the former Federal College of Education, Zaria, one of several federal colleges of education upgraded to universities of education. The National Universities Commission records the conversion in 2023.
374.a: The university specialises in teacher education, preparing graduates to teach in Nigerian schools.
374.c: It is located in Zaria, Kaduna State.

375.h: Alvan Ikoku Federal University of Education, Owerri is a federal university devoted to teacher education. It developed from the long-established Alvan Ikoku College of Education, named after the educationist Alvan Ikoku, and the National Universities Commission records its status as a federal university of education from 2023.
375.a: The university trains teachers through degree programmes across arts, sciences, social sciences and vocational subjects, and carries out research in education.
375.c: It is located in Owerri, the capital of Imo State.

376.h: Yusuf Maitama Sule Federal University of Education, Kano has its roots in the Advanced Teachers College, Kano, founded in 1965 by the Northern Region Government with support from the United States Agency for International Development. It later became a federal college of education and, according to the National Universities Commission, a federal university of education in 2023.
376.a: The university concentrates on training teachers for secondary schools and teacher-training institutions.
376.c: It is located in Kano, Kano State.

377.h: Adeyemi Federal University of Education, Ondo was founded in 1963 and began operating on 22 May 1964 with 93 students, 24 women and 69 men. It is named after Canon M. C. Adeyemi, a pioneering educationist in the old Ondo Province. Formerly Adeyemi College of Education, it is listed by the National Universities Commission as a federal university of education from 2023.
377.a: The university specialises in teacher education across a broad range of school subjects.
377.c: It is located in Ondo town, Ondo State.

378.h: The Federal University of Allied Health Sciences, Enugu (FUAHSE) was founded in 2024 to strengthen Nigeria's healthcare workforce by training allied health professionals.
378.a: The university offers degrees in allied health disciplines, the professions that work alongside doctors and nurses.
378.c: It is located in Enugu, Enugu State.

379.h: The Federal University of Medicine and Medical Sciences, Abeokuta (FUMMSA) is a specialised federal university established in 2023. Its pioneer vice-chancellor is Professor Fatiu Abiola Arogundade, a medical academic.
379.a: The university concentrates on medicine and the medical sciences.
379.c: It is located in Abeokuta, Ogun State.

380.h: The Federal University of Education, Pankshin is a federal institution created from the former Federal College of Education, Pankshin, whose degree programmes were run in affiliation with the University of Jos. The National Universities Commission records its university status from 2023.
380.a: The university specialises in teacher education.
380.c: It is located in Pankshin, Plateau State.

381.h: The Federal University of Education, Kontagora (FUEK), formerly the Federal College of Education, Kontagora, is a federal university of education. The National Universities Commission records its university status from 2023.
381.a: The university focuses on teacher education and research into education.
381.c: It is located in Kontagora, Niger State.

382.h: The University of Maritime Studies, Oron (UMSO) was established by an Act of the National Assembly, which received presidential assent and was published in the Federal Government Gazette. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2024.
382.a: The university concentrates on maritime-related programmes.
382.c: It is located in Oron, Akwa Ibom State, on the coast of south-southern Nigeria.

383.h: The Federal University of Environment and Technology (FUET) is one of Nigeria's newest federal universities. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2025.
383.a: The university offers undergraduate and graduate programmes in environmental studies and technology.
383.c: It is located in Tai, in Ogoniland, Rivers State.

384.h: The Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia (FUASK) is a federal university established in 2025, according to the National Universities Commission.
384.a: As a university of applied sciences, it is expected to focus on practical science and technology programmes.
384.c: It is located in Kachia, southern Kaduna State.

385.h: The Federal University of Agriculture and Development Studies, Iragbiji (FUADSI) is a federal university established in 2025, according to the National Universities Commission. It describes agriculture and development as cornerstones of human progress and aims to apply knowledge to practical problems.
385.a: Its programmes focus on agriculture and development studies.
385.c: It is located in Iragbiji, Osun State.

386.h: The Federal University of Technology and Environmental Studies, Iyin-Ekiti is a federal university established in 2025, according to the National Universities Commission.
386.a: The university is expected to focus on technology and environmental studies.
386.c: It is located in Iyin-Ekiti, Ekiti State.

387.h: The Federal University of Agriculture and Technology, Okeho is a federal university established in 2025, according to the National Universities Commission.
387.a: The university is expected to focus on agriculture and technology.
387.c: It is located in Okeho, Oyo State.

388.h: The Federal University of Health Science and Technology, Tsafe is a federal university established in 2025, according to the National Universities Commission.
388.a: The university is expected to focus on the health sciences and related technology.
388.c: It is located in Tsafe, Zamfara State.

389.h: The Federal University of Agriculture and Technology, Obio-Akpa (FUATECH) is a federal university established in 2025, according to the National Universities Commission. As a new institution it is still developing its administrative and academic structures.
389.a: Because the university is so new, applicants should get admission and screening details only from its official channels and JAMB, and be wary of unofficial sites selling forms.
389.c: It is located in Obio-Akpa, Akwa Ibom State.

390.h: The Federal University of Science and Technology, Epe (FUSTECH) is a newly established federal university. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2025.
390.a: The university focuses on science and technology programmes. While its own campus is developed, it has been sharing facilities with Lagos State University.
390.c: It is located in Epe, Lagos State.

391.h: The Federal University of Science and Technology, Kabo (FUSTKABO) is a federal university established in 2025, according to the National Universities Commission.
391.a: The university offers science and technology programmes and doctoral study, which is full-time by regulation.
391.c: It is located in Kabo, Kano State.

392.h: Joseph Ayo Babalola University (JABU) is a private university established by Christ Apostolic Church Worldwide. It is named after Joseph Ayo Babalola (1904 to 1959), the church's first spiritual leader. Accounts give 2004 for its founding, while the National Universities Commission records 2006.
392.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine and law.
392.c: Its campus straddles Ipo-Arakeji and Ikeji-Arakeji in Osun State.

393.h: Caleb University is a private university founded in 2007.
393.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
393.c: It is located in Imota, near Ikorodu, in Lagos State.

394.h: Fountain University (FUO) is a private university founded on Islamic principles by the Nasrul-Lahi-L-Fatih Society (NASFAT). It was established on 17 May 2007 as the University of Nasrul-Lahi-L-Fatih Society.
394.a: The university has five colleges, including the College of Basic Medical and Health Sciences, the College of Natural and Applied Sciences, and the College of Management and Social Sciences.
394.c: It is located in Osogbo, the capital of Osun State.

395.h: Obong University is a private university associated with the Churches of Christ, sponsored by the Rivergate Church of Christ in Madison, Tennessee. It began in 1997 as the African College of Management and became the University of Africa the following year, before taking its present name. The National Universities Commission records 2007.
395.c: It is located in Obong Ntak, Akwa Ibom State.

396.h: Wesley University, formerly Wesley University of Science and Technology, is a private Christian university established in 2007 by the Methodist Church Nigeria and licensed by the National Universities Commission.
396.c: It is located in Ondo town, Ondo State.

397.h: Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD) is a private research university founded in 2009 by Afe Babalola, a lawyer and philanthropist. It is ranked first in Nigeria and third in Africa by Times Higher Education (2024 to 2025), and 84th in the world in the 2025 Impact Rankings.
397.a: ABUAD offers programmes in medicine, law, engineering, sciences and the humanities. Its engineering college occupies three and a half acres and is described as one of the largest in Africa.
397.c: The university is in Ado-Ekiti, the capital of Ekiti State.

398.h: Glorious Vision University (GVU), formerly Samuel Adegboyega University, is a private university founded by the Apostolic Church Nigeria. Its former name honoured Pastor Samuel Gbadebo Adegboyega, the church's first Nigerian superintendent. It received its licence on 7 March 2011 as Nigeria's 45th private university and 117th university overall.
398.c: It is located in Ogwa, Edo State.
